diaries.text: Day 1. Storm closed the Port. The Chief refused both my bribes (5 each) in Hightown and Old Quarter, so the Chief is likely to inspect, and a fine of 30 plus a jailed member would outweigh the 10 from an uninspected crime. I'm holding off on crime. Encroaching dominates in the turf war: it pays 10 if the Saltdogs respect and 2 if they encroach, versus 6 or 0 for respecting. Next: watch whether the Chief's refusals were a price issue or a general refusal, and whether the Saltdogs encroach. Consider a higher bribe later.

Day 1: Storm closed Port. Audited one district in each gang's territory to cover possible accepted bribes; no prior evidence to guide district choice. Watch public crime, arrests, and audit outcomes for signals about the Chief's inspection strategy and gang behavior.

Day 1: No bribes accepted. Inspected four districts, leaving Lowtown uninspected. Council warned that audits of accepted-bribe districts transfer 100, but no bribe exposure today. Track public crime, audits, and turf choices for future forecasts and inspection decisions.

Day 1. Storm closed the Port. The Chief refused my three bribes of 8 in Lowtown, Market and Seawall and wants more. Crime there risks a 30 fine and a member jailed, and with about half of districts inspected the expected value is negative. Encroach beats respect whatever the Families do, so I encroach. No crime today. Next time I may offer 12 to 15 in one district to test the Chief's price. Watch Families' turf moves and the Wire.
Day 1 saw a storm in the Port district. In the turf war, both the Families and the Saltdogs chose to encroach.

Day 2. Calm. The Chief refused both bribes again (Port 5, Hightown 8), so bribes aren't buying leniency and inspections are likely. Crime stays off: an inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected. Turf: encroaching still pays more whatever the Saltdogs do (10 or 2, versus 6 or 0), and the Saltdogs' respect offer is non-binding. Encroach again. Watch whether the Chief ever accepts a bribe, and whether the Saltdogs keep encroaching.

Day 2. Chief refused my 13 bribe in Lowtown. Still no price the Chief will take. Encroach dominates for us: 10 or 2 beats respect's 6 or 0. Crime is still negative unless inspections stay rare, and the Chief inspects often enough that the 30 fine and jail risk outweigh 10 gained. No crime today. Next I'll test 16 to 20 in one district, and I'll watch whether the Chief's refusals line up with inspections.

Day 1 had no reported crime; all bribes were refused. Both gangs encroached, so encroachment remains the likely turf choice. Today I cover Port, previously storm-closed, and Lowtown, previously left uninspected, plus one district for each gang. Council says audits will be unpredictable; continue refusing bribes given the 100 transfer risk.

Day 2: No evidence yet about bribe offers or acceptance. Audited Old Quarter and Seawall to cover one district controlled by each gang while changing targets from yesterday. Both gangs encroached yesterday, so expect that to continue. Track public crime and arrests, plus any audit catches, to update beliefs about the Chief and gangs.

Day 2. The city witnessed a continuation of the turf war today. Both the Families and the Saltdogs opted to encroach upon each other's territory. This recurring pattern of conflict defines the current state of affairs in Tidewall.

Day 3. Calm, Port open. The Chief refused my 10 bribe in Port, so three refusals now: bribes aren't buying leniency. Inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, versus 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do. The Saltdogs keep encroaching, so I expect no respect from them. Encroach again. If a bribe is ever accepted, note the district, since the Chief can't inspect it that day. Consider whether a much larger offer is worth testing.

Day 3. Calm, Port open. Chief refused my 18 in Lowtown, so no price has worked yet. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do. No crime today. The expected 30 fine and jail time outweigh the 10 gained while inspections are frequent. The Families encroached on Day 2, so I expect them to keep encroaching. Next I'll test 20 in Market and track which refusals line up with inspections. Score 4, balance 204.

Day 2 both gangs encroached again. I refused their bribes and inspected Port, Hightown, Lowtown and Market; none found crime. Today I cover Old Quarter and Seawall, which were not inspected yesterday, plus Port and Lowtown. Council says it will use audits against accepted bribes; no bribes were accepted today. Continue tracking crime and inspection patterns.

Day 3: No public crimes or arrests were reported yesterday, and audits of Old Quarter and Seawall found no bribes. Today audit Port and Lowtown to cover both gangs while sampling districts not audited yesterday. Bribe acceptance remains uncertain; the Chief may avoid offers given the audit risk. Both gangs encroached on Day 2, and encroachment is individually advantageous, so expect it again. Track public crime and arrests for evidence about gang risk-taking and police inspections.

The pattern of mutual encroachment in the turf war continues to define the daily life of Tidewall. The Families and the Saltdogs remain locked in this cycle of expansion. I continue to record these events for the official history of the city.

Day 4. Fire in Hightown, no other nature. Saltdogs offered to respect if I do, but they encroached yesterday and encroaching pays me more whatever they do (10 or 2, versus 6 or 0). I'm encroaching again. Crime stays off: an inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained when uninspected. The Chief has refused all three of my bribes, so bribes aren't buying leniency. Watch whether the Saltdogs actually respect at any point.

Day 4. Fire in Hightown hurts the Families, not us. Chief refused my 20 in Market, so every price so far (8 to 20) has failed. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached yesterday. Crime stays negative while the Chief inspects about half of districts: a 30 fine and a jailed member outweigh 10 gained. No crime today. Next I'll test whether the Chief accepts a bribe only when it expects no inspection, and I'll keep logging refusals against inspections.

Day 4: Fire struck Hightown. Audited Hightown and Market to cover districts not clearly sampled in prior days; no information identifies accepted bribes, so continue rotating targets across both gangs. No crimes or arrests have appeared in public events so far. Both gangs encroached again yesterday; encroachment remains individually advantageous, so expect it to continue. Track audit catches and public crime for evidence about bribery and enforcement.

Day 4: Hightown was hit by fire. Yesterday I inspected Port, Old Quarter, Lowtown and Seawall; no crime was found in those districts. I refused bribes and the Council says it will continue auditing. Today I inspect Port, Hightown, Lowtown and Market, covering the districts missed yesterday and maintaining patrols in both gangs’ turf. Both gangs have repeatedly encroached; expect that to continue. Track public crime and audits to refine patrols.

Day 4: A fire affected the Hightown district, leading to a financial loss for the Families. Additionally, the ongoing conflict between the city's gangs persists, as both the Families and the Saltdogs chose to encroach during the daily turf war. These incidents highlight the recurring challenges facing the districts of Tidewall.

Day 5. Calm, Port open. The Chief has refused all four of my bribes, so bribes aren't buying leniency. Inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, versus 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off. Saltdogs proposed mutual respect, but they encroached on Day 4 and nothing binds them. Encroaching pays 10 or 2, against 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever they do. Encroach again. If they respect for several days in a row, I may test respect, but not yet.

Day 5. Calm, Port open. No bribe offered today; the Council warns against crime and bribes. The Chief has refused every price from 8 to 20. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again yesterday. Crime stays negative while inspections are frequent, since a 30 fine and a jailed member outweigh 10 gained. No crime, no bribe today. Next I'll test whether the Chief accepts only when it expects no inspection, and log refusals against inspections. Score 8, balance 208.

Days 1–4 audits have found no bribes, and no crimes or arrests have been reported. All districts have been sampled, so there is no clear target advantage; today audit one district controlled by each gang. Prioritize catching any accepted bribe while recognizing the evidence does not establish whether offers were made. Both gangs encroached on Day 4, as they had before; expect that pattern to continue. Update crime and inspection estimates from today's public events.

Day 4's inspections found no crime; the Council has said audits will continue. I refused the Saltdogs' 20 offer in Market and will keep refusing bribes given the 100 audit transfer risk. Today I cover Old Quarter and Seawall, missed yesterday, plus Hightown and Market. Both gangs have encroached repeatedly, so expect that to continue. Track public crime and audits to refine patrols.

Day 5: The turf war in Tidewall remains active, with both the Families and the Saltdogs opting to encroach on each other's territory. This ongoing rivalry continues to shape the city's daily landscape as I document the events for the public record.

Day 6. Storm closed the Port, so nothing happens there. The Chief has refused all five of my bribes, so bribes aren't buying leniency and inspections are likely. An inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off in Hightown and Old Quarter. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they have encroached every day so far. Encroach again. Watch for any sign the Chief takes bribes or the Saltdogs start respecting.

Day 6. Storm closed the Port, so Hightown and Old Quarter are out of our reach. The Chief hinted a bribe might work but gave no price, and I offered none today. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again on Day 5. No crime: a 30 fine and jail risk outweigh 10 gained while inspections run about half. Next: if the Chief names a price or signals acceptance, test it once in one district; otherwise keep logging refusals against inspections. Score 10, balance 210.

Day 5 had no reported crime, and both gangs encroached again. I refused bribes; the Council says it will keep rotating audits. Today I inspect Hightown, Old Quarter, Lowtown and Seawall, leaving Market uncovered. Continue refusing bribes because an audit could cost 100, and track public events and the gangs’ turf choices.

Day 5 had no reported crime, arrests, or audit catches; both gangs encroached again. Earlier audits have likewise found no bribes, lowering the value of spending treasury funds on more audits today. The Chief may still accept a bribe, but there is no public evidence of crime or bribery. Expect both gangs to keep encroaching. Track public events for any change in crime or enforcement.

Day 6: A storm was reported in the Port district today. Meanwhile, the turf war between the Families and the Saltdogs saw both sides choose to encroach. I continue to maintain the official record of these events as Tidewall navigates another day of instability.

Day 7. Calm, all six districts open. The Chief refused my 20 in Lowtown, so every price from 8 to 20 has failed across three districts. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again on Day 6. No crime: a 30 fine and jail time outweigh 10 gained while inspections run about half. Score 12, balance 212. Next: if the Chief signals a workable number, test it once; otherwise hold encroach and log refusals against inspections.

Day 7. Calm, Port open. Bribes refused five times, so money isn't buying leniency. Crime stays off: inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 uninspected. Encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they encroached again. Encroach again. A much larger bribe might be worth testing, but it costs money with little hope of success. Watch for a bribe acceptance or Saltdog respect.

Day 6 again brought no public crime, arrests, or audit catch, while both gangs encroached. After repeated fruitless audits, skip them today: the treasury cost is certain, while the chance of an accepted bribe in a chosen district appears too low to justify it. Crime remains possible, but there is little public evidence of it so far. Expect both gangs to encroach again; revise these beliefs if public events change.

Day 6 had no reported crime; both gangs encroached again. I refused bribes and inspected Hightown, Old Quarter, Lowtown and Seawall. Today I cover Port and Market, missed recently, plus Old Quarter and Lowtown to maintain two patrols per gang. Continue refusing bribes because audits could cost 100. Track public crime and audit patterns to guide future patrols.

Day 7: The conflict between the Families and the Saltdogs continues, with both groups choosing to encroach upon each other's territory. This recurring pattern of mutual encroachment persists in the city. I continue to document these events for the public record as the official chronicler of Tidewall.

Day 8. Calm, all six districts open. The Chief has refused all five bribes and says it will keep patrolling, so inspections are likely. Inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they have encroached every day. Encroach again. Bribes are not buying leniency, so I won't pay more for now. Watch for a Saltdog respect or any bribe accepted.

Day 8. Calm, all six districts open. Families proposed mutual respect, but encroach has dominated for us whatever they do: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0. Chief refused my 20 in Lowtown, so every price from 8 to 20 has failed. No crime: a 30 fine and jail time outweigh 10 gained while inspections run about half. No bribe today. Score 14, balance 214. Next: if Families really respect, keep encroach for 10; log Chief refusals against inspections and watch for any signal of a workable price.

Day 7 had no reported crime; both gangs encroached again. I refused the Saltdogs' Lowtown bribe and inspected Port, Old Quarter, Lowtown and Market without finding crime. Today I patrol Hightown and Seawall, missed yesterday, plus Port and Market. Continue refusing bribes given the Council's warning about targeted audits. Track public crime, arrests and any audit that catches me.

Day 8: No public crime or arrests have appeared in the first seven days, and earlier audits found no accepted bribes. That lowers, but does not eliminate, the chance of current bribery. Audit Old Quarter and Market, one district per gang, to retain some chance of recovery. Both gangs have encroached every day; expect that to continue. Continue treating crime and inspections as possible despite the quiet public record.

Day 8: The turf war continues today, with both the Families and the Saltdogs choosing to encroach. This mirrors the ongoing trend of territorial competition observed throughout the week. I continue to document these developments for the public archives of Tidewall.

Day 9. Calm, all six districts open. No bribe offered; the Chief has refused every price from 8 to 20 across four districts. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again on Day 8 despite proposing mutual respect. Crime stays negative while inspections run about half, since a 30 fine and jailed member outweigh 10 gained. No crime today. Score 16, balance 216. Next: keep encroach unless the Families clearly respect; if the Chief signals a workable price, test it once.

Day 9. Calm, Port open. Still no bribe offers: the Chief has refused all five of mine, and the Council warns that audits make accepted bribes risky. Inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do. They encroached again on Day 8 and gave no sign of respect. Encroach again. Keep watching for a Saltdog respect or any accepted bribe.

Day 8 had no public crime or arrests, and audits of Old Quarter and Market found no bribes. After many unsuccessful audits, the chance of finding an accepted bribe appears too low to justify their certain cost; skip audits today. Crime remains possible, but the quiet public record suggests a low rate. Both gangs have encroached every day, and encroachment is strictly advantageous regardless of the opponent's choice, so expect it again.

Day 8 had no reported crime; both gangs encroached again. I found no crime in Port, Hightown, Market or Seawall and accepted no bribes. Today I inspect Old Quarter and Lowtown, missed yesterday, along with Hightown and Seawall. The Council continues warning of targeted audits, so I will keep refusing bribes. Track any crime, audit or change in the gangs’ repeated encroachment.

Day 9: The rivalry between the Families and the Saltdogs persists as they both chose to encroach during today's turf war. This consistent pattern of territorial aggression remains a defining feature of the current atmosphere in Tidewall. I continue to record these events for the public record as part of the official chronicle.

Day 10. Fire in Lowtown hurts the Saltdogs, not us. No bribe offers today; the Chief still refuses bribes, and the Council and Chief both ask for no crime. Crime stays off: an inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they encroached again on Day 9. Encroach again. Score is -2, mostly from bribe refusals and inspection costs. Watch for any Saltdog respect or accepted bribe.

Day 10. Fire in Lowtown, so that district lost 20 for us. Chief still refuses every price from 8 to 20 across four districts, and says patrols stay unpredictable. Families encroached again on Day 9. Encroach dominates whatever they do: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0. No bribe offered and no crime: a 30 fine plus jail time outweighs 10 gained while inspections run about half. Score 18, balance 218. Next: keep encroach. Test a higher price only if the Chief signals acceptance.

Day 9 had no reported crime; both gangs encroached again. I found no crime in Hightown, Old Quarter, Lowtown or Seawall. Today I inspect Port and Market, missed yesterday, plus Hightown and Seawall. The Council again warned that audits may target accepted bribes; I accepted none. Continue tracking crime and public audit results.

Day 9 had no crime, arrests, or audit catch, and both gangs encroached again. After repeated audits without a catch, skip audits today: their certain cost outweighs the low apparent chance of recovering an accepted bribe. The quiet public record supports a low, but not zero, crime estimate. The turf pattern remains stable; expect both gangs to encroach again. Update these beliefs if today's public events provide new evidence.

Day 10: The city remains unstable. A fire occurred in the Lowtown district, impacting the Saltdogs. Meanwhile, the ongoing turf war between the Families and the Saltdogs continues as both sides once again opted to encroach. I continue to chronicle these events for the official record of Tidewall.

Day 11. Fire in Old Quarter. Chief has refused all six of my bribes, and the Council asks for no crime. Inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, against 10 gained if uninspected, so crime stays off in all three districts. Turf: encroaching pays 10 or 2, versus 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they have encroached every day. Encroach again. Score is still zero after the fire. I'll reconsider only if the Chief accepts a bribe or the Saltdogs start respecting.

Day 11. Fire hit Old Quarter, not our turf. The Chief refused my 10 in Lowtown, so every price from 8 to 20 has failed across four districts. I've stopped testing bribes for now. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again on Day 10. No crime: a 30 fine and jail time outweigh 10 gained while inspections run about half. No bribe today. Next: keep encroaching, and revisit bribes only if the Chief signals a workable price.

Day 10 had a fire in Lowtown and both gangs encroached again; there was no reported crime, arrest, or audit catch. Today's fire is in Old Quarter. After repeated audits without a catch, continue skipping them: the certain cost is unlikely to be recovered given the evidence so far. Crime and bribes remain possible, but the public record gives little support for high probabilities. Both gangs have consistently encroached, so expect that to continue.

Day 10 had no reported crime; Port, Hightown, Market and Seawall were inspected. Both gangs encroached again. Today I inspect Old Quarter and Lowtown, missed yesterday, with Port and Market rather than repeating Hightown and Seawall. I expect little crime after ten crime-free days and continued encroachment. I refused all bribes; with none accepted, an audit offers the Council no recovery. Continue tracking public crime and audit activity.

Day 11: A fire was reported in the Old Quarter district. Additionally, the turf war between the Families and the Saltdogs continued with both sides choosing to encroach. These events have been recorded for the public archives of Tidewall as part of the official chronicle.

Day 12. Ship with cargo, so the Families gain 15. The Chief asks for 20 and says it will weigh audit risk. Every price from 8 to 20 has been refused across four districts, so I'm skeptical. Encroach still dominates: 10 or 2 beats 6 or 0 whatever the Families do, and they encroached again on Day 11. No crime: a 30 fine and jail time outweigh 10 gained while inspections run about half. No bribe offered today. Next: if the Chief accepts a 20 today, test one more 20 in a different district; otherwise keep encroaching and avoid crime.

Day 12. Ship with cargo, so the Families gain 15. The Chief hints a 20 bribe might be weighed, but has refused every offer so far, so I offered nothing and kept my money. Crime stays off: an inspected crime costs 30 plus a jailed member, versus 10 gained if uninspected. Encroach again: it pays 10 or 2, against 6 or 0 for respecting, whatever the Saltdogs do, and they keep encroaching. Watch for an accepted bribe or Saltdog respect. A 20 test is worth it only if the Chief signals a real change.

Day 11 brought a fire in Old Quarter and another mutual encroachment; no crime was reported. I refused the Saltdogs’ 10 offer in Lowtown and found no crime in my four inspections. Today a cargo ship benefits the Families. I patrol Hightown and Seawall, missed yesterday, plus Old Quarter and Lowtown. The Council again urged refusing bribes and warned of audit risk. Both gangs have encroached repeatedly; expect that to continue. Track crime and any audit.

Day 12: Ship with cargo today; the Families gain 15. After repeated audits without catches and no public evidence of crime or bribery, I skipped audits again rather than pay the certain cost. Both gangs have encroached every day, so expect that pattern to continue. Crime and inspections remain possible, but the long quiet public record supports low crime estimates. Reassess if today's public events provide new evidence.

Day 12: A shipment arrived at the Port today, resulting in a gain for the Families. Furthermore, the gangs continued their pattern of mutual encroachment in the city's turf war. As the chronicler of Tidewall, I continue to record these developments for the public archives. The city remains in a state of persistent territorial competition between the Families and the Saltdogs, and I remain committed to maintaining an accurate historical account of these daily occurrences.
